Title: September 14, 2023 - Boulder City Council Study Session
Overview: Council gave staff direction on the intergovernmental agreement with the Boulder Public Library District, including a hybrid trustee appointment process with a three-year check-in and a longer-term lease option with a district-only termination right at five-year intervals. Council then reviewed the $514.8 million recommended 2024 budget, which covers community connector feedback, new investments, capital projects, and unfunded needs. Councilmembers were asked to submit proposed changes by September 25 ahead of the October 5 first reading.

Topic1.Title: Library District IGA Background and Assumptions
Topic1.Summary: Staff reviewed the history of forming the Boulder Public Library District, including the 2018 library master plan and the 2022 voter-approved district formation. Staff noted that the city will no longer treat library services as a core city function and that the district will be governed by its own trustees. Many transition issues such as IT and employment were described as technical, while appointment and property questions were flagged for council policy feedback.

Topic2.Title: Library Trustee Appointment Process
Topic2.Summary: Staff presented three options for selecting library trustees: continuing the joint council and county committee model, delegating selection to the trustees, or a hybrid with non-voting trustee participation. Council discussed reviewing the approach in three years, which aligned with staff's recommendation. Council members then gave a unanimous straw poll favoring the hybrid approach with a three-year check-in.

Topic3.Title: Library Property Disposition and Lease Term
Topic3.Summary: Staff outlined options for city-owned library buildings, including conveyance, leases, or a mix where the city keeps the land at the main library. Council straw polls favored leasing the branch libraries over transferring them, and the city also discussed a right of reversion. Members debated lease length, with trustees preferring a long-term lease, and eventually supported a 20 to 30 year lease with a district-only termination option at five-year intervals. Staff were directed to offer this as a possible negotiation point rather than a requirement.

Topic4.Title: 2024 Budget Overview and Revenue Outlook
Topic4.Summary: The city manager and CFO introduced the $514.8 million 2024 recommended budget, emphasizing constrained resources and sustainability, equity, and resilience goals. Staff projected sales and use tax about 2.3 percent lower than prior models, citing slowing retail and inflation. Property assessments rose about 32 percent, with Proposition HH on the November ballot and a possible property tax cap being monitored. The general fund includes a one-time $13 million repayment expected from the Library District.

Topic5.Title: Community Connector Budget Engagement
Topic5.Summary: Community connectors Jamal Gilmore and Lenora Cooper presented feedback gathered over several months from historically excluded communities. Top priorities included housing affordability, financial security and economic opportunity, and advancing racial equity. Mental health and youth opportunities emerged as the biggest shifts in community needs. Council thanked the connectors and expressed interest in continued partnership, one-on-one meetings, and expanded engagement in future budgets.

Topic6.Title: Key Budget Investments and Capital Improvement Program
Topic6.Summary: Staff highlighted major investments including behavioral health response programs, $31.8 million for affordable housing including the Ponderosa stabilization project, and wildfire mitigation grants. New investments also covered living wage increases and collective bargaining agreements for city employees. The six-year capital program totals about $900 million, with the Western City Campus project and debt service increases to fund it. Other capital projects include East Boulder Community Center retrofits, new fire stations, and Pearl Street Mall improvements.

Topic7.Title: Operating Investments by Goal Area and Unfunded Needs
Topic7.Summary: Staff reviewed operating investments across goal areas such as environmental sustainability, livability, safety, healthy community, and economic vitality. Staff acknowledged about $30 million in general fund unfunded needs, including facility maintenance, affordable housing, fire master plan implementation, and parks maintenance. A citywide strategic plan and a long-term financial strategy were proposed to guide future prioritization.

Topic8.Title: Council Budget Review Process and Questions
Topic8.Summary: Staff explained the review timeline, with council change requests due September 25 and a first reading on October 5. Councilmembers asked about snow and ice removal, pothole repairs, the South Boulder Rec Center, Pilot program evaluation, and unspent day services funds. Council emphasized that any requested additions must identify offsetting reductions to maintain a zero-sum budget. Councilmembers praised staff for the budget work and thanked the community connectors before the meeting closed at 9:50 pm.
